sources.title: CVE-2016-5734: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: phpMyAdmin 4.0.x before 4.0.10.16, 4.4.x before 4.4.15.7, and 4.6.x before 4.6.3 does not properly choose delimiters to prevent use of the preg_replace e (aka eval) modifier, which might allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code via a crafted string, as demonstrated by the table search-and-replace implementation.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2016-5734 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2005-4349: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: SQL injection vulnerability in server_privileges.php in phpMyAdmin 2.7.0 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary SQL commands via the (1) dbname and (2) checkprivs parameters.  NOTE: the vendor and a third party have disputed this issue, saying that the main task of the program is to support query execution by authenticated users, and no external attack scenario exists without an auto-login configuration.  Thus it is likely that this issue will be REJECTED.  However, a closely related CSRF issue has been assigned CVE-2005-4450
supports: NVD lists CVE-2005-4349 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

An SQL injection vulnerability has been discovered where certain parameters are not ... | Webpage text: Announcement-ID: PMASA-2020-3 SQL injection relating to searching An SQL injection vulnerability has been discovered where certain parameters are not properly escaped when generating certain queries for search actions within phpMyAdmin. An attacker can generate specially-crafted database or table names. The attack can be performed if a user attempts certain search operations on the malicious database or table. Because of the specific steps required to exploit this, we consider this vulnerability to be of moderate severity. phpMyAdmin 4.9.x releases prior to 4.9.5 and the 5.0.x releases prior to 5.0.2 are affected. Upgrade to phpMyAdmin 4.9.5 or 5.0.2 or newer or apply patch listed below. Thanks to hoangn144_VCS and Yutaka WATANABE for reporting these vulnerabilities. Originally published in July 2023. Updated September 2025. OS Command Injection is a web application vulnerability that can lead to arbitrary command execution on the underlying operating system. Attackers exploit command injection vulnerabilities by supplying malicious input to operating system commands executed by an application. Successful exploitation can allow attackers to retrieve sensitive data, escalate privileges, and move laterally within a network. Strong input validation is the preferred defense against command injection vulnerabilities. Avoiding operating system command execution entirely is the most effective mitigation. What is OS Command Injection? OS Command Injection is a web application vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system. Because successful exploitation can lead to full command execution on a target system, command injection vulnerabilities are often considered among the most severe web application vulnerabilities. For a concise definition, see Fastly's Learning Center entry on OS Command Injection. This is a common pattern in web applications that perform operating system command execution on behalf of users, and it can become dangerous when user input is passed directly to shell commands.
